questions.question: What is Brownian motion defined as?
options: The random motion of particles suspended in a medium
The movement of particles down a concentration gradient
The process of a solid turning into a gas
The reaction of an acid with a metal

questions.question: How does increasing the temperature affect the particles in a gas or solution?
options: They move more slowly
They stop moving entirely
They move more quickly
They clump together and freeze

questions.question: Why are suspensions not classified as solutions?
options: They are always made of pure substances
Solid particles can be seen in them and will eventually settle over time
They can never be separated by filtration
They have a fixed boiling point like pure materials

questions.question: What must be overcome for a solute to dissolve in a solvent?
options: The gravitational pull on the liquid
The forces of attraction between solute particles
The chemical bonds within the oxygen atoms
The atmospheric pressure of the room

questions.question: Why might the total volume of a mixture of two different liquids be less than expected?
options: Some particles are destroyed during mixing
The particles expand and take up more space
One type of particle can fit into the spaces between the other type
The liquids undergo a gas-producing chemical reaction

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding dissolving and melting?
options: Dissolving is a chemical change while melting is a physical change
They are completely identical processes
Dissolving is not the same as melting, but both are physical processes
Melting requires a solvent while dissolving does not

questions.question: Why should scientific methods be written clearly and concisely?
options: So that they are both repeatable and reproducible
To prevent other scientists from understanding the results
To ensure the investigation cannot be copied
So that they only contain theoretical predictions

questions.question: What is formed when a soluble solid dissolves in an appropriate solvent?
options: A suspension
A pure material
A solution
An element

questions.question: If you mix 15 g of sugar into 200 g of water, what will be the total mass of the mixture?
options: 215 g, because mass is conserved
Less than 200 g, because sugar loses mass when it dissolves
Exactly 185 g, because sugar takes up volume
More than 215 g, because of chemical reactions

questions.question: Which piece of equipment and unit are typically used to measure liquid volume in a lab?
options: A balance, in grams (g)
A measuring cylinder, in cm³
A thermometer, in degrees Celsius (°C)
A ruler, in millimetres (mm)

questions.question: What is a characteristic property of a pure material?
options: It has a fixed melting point and boiling point
It melts and boils over a wide range of temperatures
It can be easily separated by simple filtration
It is always made of several different types of substances

questions.question: What effect do impurities have on the melting and boiling points of a material?
options: They make the melting and boiling points completely unpredictable
They change the melting and boiling point of the material
They have absolutely no effect on either point
They make the melting and boiling points exactly the same temperature

questions.question: What can happen to dissolved solutes as a hot solution cools down?
options: They may become insoluble and settle out
They will turn into a gas and evaporate
They will permanently disappear
They will become more soluble

questions.question: How can a line of best fit on a graph be useful?
options: It shows how to change the independent variable
It can help to identify and describe relationships between variables
It is used to make sure the experiment is a fair test
It indicates the exact mass of the solute used

questions.question: In a fair test, why is only the variable being tested changed?
options: To make the experiment run faster
So that it is clear that only this variable made a difference to the results
To keep the temperature of the laboratory constant
To make the graph easier to plot by hand
